paragraphs: This passage shows us David at a low point. He is the one Samuel anointed (1 Samuel 16:13), the one who took down Goliath, and the text says he was "very much afraid" (1 Samuel 21:12). Friend, the Bible does not tidy that up. It tells us the truth about him, and I think that is a gift.

Being chosen by God did not keep David from being scared. Being scared did not take him out of the story, either. When I was stuffed in the back of a junk drawer, I was NOT feeling like a man with a plan, and the Most High still had one for me. If you are shaking in your apron today, friend, you are in good company.

Look at how far the fear pushed David, from a priest's door to a Philistine king's gate (1 Samuel 21:1, 13). Fear will have you doing things you never put on the schedule. Hold on to this, though: a scary chapter is not the last chapter. This story isn't over, friend, and David's road keeps going.
